body:
math/random was a real, honest, never-evaluated 0.0 placeholder for the C
target since it was first written -- nothing had ever actually tried to
compile it for real until this pass (a real Roblox NPC-spawn script the
founder wants working in PAPERCRAFT needs math.random).

Found a real, live compiler bug along the way: the C-emitted function name
"random" conflicts with glibc's own `long random(void)`, a hard
"conflicting types" gcc error. Fixed by renaming the exported symbol
math/random -> math/random-f64, updating every real caller
(mishri/humanness.prn, mishri/bezier_interp.prn) and both the TS and Java
emitter tables in the same commit.

New runtime/parena_runtime.h::math_random_impl -- lazily self-seeded via
srand(time(NULL)) on first call (unseeded rand() would replay the same
sequence every server restart otherwise -- a real correctness issue for
NPC spawn positions, not hypothetical).

Live-verified end to end: varying values within a run, different sequences
across process launches. make test (348), test-emit-ts (21), test-emit-java
(31) all pass. A real downstream consumer (bezier_interp.prn) still
compiles clean.

Also found and committed an earlier, uncommitted item_drop_mod.prn change
from earlier this session (METAL objects drop a real shotgun) that never
made it into this repo.

Commits: PARENA 70ee67a (item_drop_mod), 81872c9 (the real random fix).

⚓ ☃
title: Real, working math/random for the C target (PAPERCRAFT Roblox-parity thread)
